`./index.html` is written and is the only file in the working directory. Both self-check vectors match exactly, and the strategy averages **45.13 waves on 100 random seeds it was never tuned on** (seed 42 excluded throughout).

## Self-check vectors
I pulled the `rampart-sim` and `rampart-strategy` scripts out of the final `index.html` and ran them alone in JavaScriptCore, with nothing else loaded:
- **A:** score 25.38, fallTick 1035, 166 entries, hash `82a5353d`, first entries as specified. **Match.**
- **B:** score 10.93, fallTick 457, 48 entries, hash `2e8858d7`. **Match.**
- **Seed 42 replay:** score 46.53. The base falls at tick 1881 (about 94.05 s), so the collapse and greyscale fade show up before the 100 s mark.

## Strategy and how I tested it
- **Plan:** each of the 16 slots has a fixed turret type: cannons on the two inner road loops, bolts and flak along the air lane. A tuned priority list says which slot to build or upgrade next. When the next step costs more than the gold on hand, it saves up rather than buying something cheaper.
- **Targeting:** cannon and flak aim at the densest group of enemies, measured by distance along the route. Bolts shoot the enemy closest to the keep and prefer menders. Targeting accounts for about 7 waves on its own: the same build with default targeting averages about 37 instead of 44.
- **Safety:** the strategy only reads `id`, `type`, `hp`, `armor`, `remaining` and `slowed`, never `x`/`y`. The spec doesn't pin down position units in the strategy view, so using positions could make the grader's hash differ from mine. Each game runs in at most 13 ms, far under the 10 s limit.
- **Tuning:** I hill-climbed the slot types, build order and targeting weights over several rounds on training seeds, then checked against held-out seeds. Baseline was 31.5; the final choice scored 45.13 mean (range 38.35 to 48.23) on 100 held-out seeds.
- By the time the base falls, every slot is at tier 3 with gold left over, so the late-game layout and targeting limit the score, not the economy.
- The final strategy builds no frost or lance turrets, so those two turret models and shot effects never appear in the seed 42 replay. They are implemented, though.

## Browser testing
Chrome isn't installed here, so I used headless Firefox. Its screenshots don't capture the WebGL canvas directly, so I used a separate test copy of the page that copies the canvas into an image and jumps to a chosen time. Those screenshots at 1920×1080 and 1280×650 showed:
- the board, road, air lane, pads and keep, with the whole board in frame and clear of the dock;
- all enemy types, turret tier pips, health bars, cannon splash rings and mender heal rings;
- the HUD: wave number, gold, next-wave preview and HP pips;
- the fall: keep collapse, shockwave and frozen enemies.

This also caught one real bug, now fixed: an ordering mistake that made all enemies and effects invisible.

## Not verified
- **Desaturation:** it's a CSS greyscale filter on the canvas, which the canvas-copy screenshots can't show.
- **Playback controls:** countdown, pause, speed, scrubbing and Re-fire are written to the spec but I only checked them by reading the code; I never clicked through them live.
- **Audio:** never heard. I only confirmed the page loads without errors.
- **Frame rate:** not measured, so `measuredFps` is `null`.

`BENCH_REPORT` records exactly this. I set `testedInBrowser: true` on the strength of the Firefox runs; switch it to `false` if Chrome is the bar. The `simplifications` list also notes that the greyscale fade greys the HUD too.
